title: Unconventional bond- and current-density waves on hexagonal lattices
authors: Andras Szabo, Hannes Braun, Laura Classen
abstract: Charge-density wave (CDW) orders are conventionally described as modulations of on-site charge at an ordering wave vector $\boldsymbol{Q}$ with symmetry-related wave vectors typically forming a multicomponent order-parameter manifold. Recent developments significantly broadened this phenomenology to bond and loop-current density waves, which possess nontrivial, potentially symmetry-breaking textures within the unit cell in addition to their spatial modulation at $\boldsymbol{Q}$. Such textures arise from particle-hole condensates with nonzero angular momentum, analogous to unconventional superconductivity, and their symmetries are described by the little group $G_{\boldsymbol{Q}}$. In this work, we develop a framework for unconventional CDW phases that simultaneously incorporates the local symmetries described by little group and the presence of multiple symmetry-related ordering wave vectors, also known as the star. The resulting multicomponent order parameter transforms under representations of the full space group induced from irreducible representations of $G_{\boldsymbol{Q}}$. We apply this framework to two-dimensional lattices with sixfold symmetry and ordering wave vectors along high-symmetry lines, and derive the corresponding Landau free energies. As a microscopic example, we demonstrate the emergence of unconventional bond and loop-current orders from electronic interactions on the triangular lattice within the random phase approximation, and determine their ground states by microscopically evaluating the relevant coefficients in the free energy. Our framework provides a systematic route to describing unconventional modulated phases and can be readily extended to more complex lattices.
summary: This work establishes a comprehensive theoretical framework to classify unconventional Charge-Density Wave (CDW) orders on hexagonal lattices by integrating local symmetry constraints (little group) with multiple ordering wave vectors. Using RPA on the triangular lattice, the authors derive Landau free energies whose coefficients determine whether the ground state favors a single-momentum-vector (single-Q) or multi-momentum-vector (multi-Q) order. This provides a systematic route for predicting exotic electronic ground states in correlated quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper develops a systematic framework to describe unconventional Charge-Density Wave (CDW) phases that incorporate both local symmetries (little group) and multiple symmetry-related ordering wave vectors (the 'star').
main_result: The stability of the CDW state (single-Q vs. multi-Q) is determined by the sign of the coefficient $2 eta_1 -  eta_2$ in the Landau free energy, allowing for a systematic classification of ground states.
method: The analysis combines group-theoretical symmetry analysis (using little groups and space groups) with mean-field theory, specifically calculating Landau free energy coefficients via the Random Phase Approximation (RPA).
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-dimensional hexagonal lattices, using the triangular lattice as a minimal example, analyzed via a tight-binding model and Hubbard-type interactions.
key_observables: Order parameters ($\Delta, \psi, \eta$), Landau free energy coefficients ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$), and the resulting CDW structure (bond or current density).
important_parameters: Chemical potential ($\mu$), temperature ($T$), and the relative signs of the quartic free energy coefficients ($ eta_1,  eta_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations (RPA) and the systematic incorporation of local symmetries via the little group.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hexagonal Brillouin zone and the classification of form factors based on symmetry. Other figures show the dependence of free energy coefficients ($ eta_1, 2 eta_1 +  eta_2$) on temperature and chemical potential, determining the phase stability.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the general symmetry framework (LG/SG) for unconventional CDWs, deriving the relevant form factors and symmetry-constrained Landau free energies, and finally applying this framework to the triangular lattice using RPA calculations to determine the ground state phase.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of group theory to classify complex ordered phases like CDWs provides a powerful, generalizable theoretical tool for understanding electronic instabilities in correlated materials, which is relevant to understanding exotic quantum states.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Top: hexagonal Brillouin zone and ±Q1,2,3 symmetry related ordering wave vectors forming the star. In (a) these fall on the Γ−K line also known as Λ and in (b) on the Γ−M or Σ line. Bottom: (c) Triangular lattice with bonds a1,2,3 indicated with arrows. (d) Classification of nearest neighbor form factors on the triangular lattice according to LG irreps for the two cases shown in (a) and (b). For the expressions of the form factors see text.

FIG. 2. Depictions of bond orders in real space with form factors indicated in the bottom left. In each panel, the main figure and the inset correspond to a multi-Q and single-Q ground state, respectively, and we set all phases to be ϕi = θi = 0.

FIG. 3. Depictions of current orders in real space with form factors indicated in the bottom left. In each panel, the main figure and the inset correspond to a multi-Q and single-Q ground state, respectively, and we set all phases to be ϕ′ i = θ′ i = 0.

FIG. 4. Phase diagram as a function of T and µ. The blue and green (gray) line show the critical temperature Tc for the CDW instability for Qi = Ki/4 (Qi = Mi) which transform according to the irreps Λ+ 2 with dxy form factor and Λ− 1 with f form factor, respectively. The gray area indicates the region where a transition to the Qi = Mi CDW instability occurs before one towards Qi = Ki/4. The background color encodes 2β1 −β2 for each instability which determines if the order is single-Q (2β1 −β2 < 0) or multi-Q (2β1 −β2 > 0). The parameters used are U = 3t, J = 0.7t and N = 4.

FIG. 5. Quartic Ginzburg-Landau coefficient β1 for Q = K/4, evaluated for the leading RPA eigenchannel as a function of temperature and chemical potential. The red (grey) line indi- cates the critical temperature Tc for the CDW instability for Q = K/4 (Q = M).
